newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Environment spending to generate jobs - Swedish PM.
newsitem.headline: Environment spending to generate jobs - Swedish PM.

text.p: Sweden's Prime Minister said on Friday that the 10 billion crowns his government plans to invest in environmental measures over three years will result in private investments of around 30 billion crowns.
"A cautious estimate is that it concerns private investments of about 30 billion crowns," Persson told a seminar. "This will create many jobs."
Persson also expected that public spending on the environment would increase after the year 2000.
"I think it will increase," he said. "If I were able to make a decision about the year 2001 now, I would put additional money here (on the environment)."
Persson also said his minority Social Democratic government would invest in construction projects.

He mentioned a tunnel in the southern city of Malmo, an improved west coast railway between Gothenburg and Oslo, in Norway, another track on the Stockholm subway and a railway, Botniabanan, between Sundsvall and Umea in the north east.
"All these projects will now start," he said, adding that they would create new jobs.
"When the Botniabanan is finished, investments in that alone will total more than 10 billion crowns and thousands of man years of work," he said.

The construction is in line with budget leaks saying the government's April 15 budget proposal will contain construction projects in an attempt for Persson to keep his pledge to halve unemployment to four percent by the year 2000.
In March, 8.4 percent of the Swedish work force was unemployed.
